Subject: Re: Question from today’s discovery — deletion/backup timelines

Jordan — great questions. Per our call notes, I wanted to capture next steps and give a conservative view of how our deletion/RTBF flow behaves across layers.

Short answers (high level):
- Active storage: delete API triggers immediate logical deletion (records marked/removed from live indexes within seconds to minutes, depending on batch windows).
- Backups/snapshots: nightly snapshots are immutable by default. Typical snapshot retention is 30 days; restores of snapshots could temporarily re-introduce data unless filtered. We can discuss an expedited snapshot purge process for named accounts.
- Replicas/replication lag: usually caught up within minutes; nothing more than a few hours in worst case.
- Region: data is stored per-region; RTBF requests scoped to a region will only affect that region’s storage/backups unless cross-region replication is enabled.

Action items I’ll take:
1) Internal runbook with exact steps and estimated timelines (I’ll attach a summary).
2) Confirm with infra if we can offer a 7-day expedited backup purge for enterprise customers (may require ticket + consent).
3) Provide redline-free language for your legal team describing our delete API and backup constraints.

Could you confirm whether you need EU-only purges or both EU + US? I’ll pull in engineering on any immediate exceptions.

Thanks — Camila

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: internal: FintechCo RTBF backup purge question

Camila / David — quick internal notes after looking at infra: 
- Active delete path: delete API writes tombstones to the metadata table; index compactions remove docs on next maintenance window (typically within 1–6 hours, but can be tuned per account).
- Backups: we take incremental daily snapshots to S3 with a 30-day lifecycle by default. Snapshots are immutable; to guarantee removal we would need to either delete snapshot objects (requires S3 delete and possible retention lock checks) or create a replace-restore workflow (restore day N, scrub data, re-snapshot). Both have operational cost.
- Faster option: we can add account to an accelerated purge queue — we’ll create a support ticket and run a manual snapshot prune. Requires ops approval and a signed request from customer.
- KMS/HSM note: if customer keys are involved (customer-managed KMS), we can also revoke keys to render backups unreadable — legal may consider that a destructive action.

Estimate for FintechCo (conservative):
- Logical removal from live indexes: 0–1 hour
- Compaction to purge tombstones: up to 6 hours
- Replica convergence: up to 2 hours
- Backup object deletion (with accelerated process): 3–7 days (depends on approvals)

I’ll draft a short consumer-friendly paragraph for legal to include in the DPA.

— Mateo

Jordan — thanks for confirming on the call that FintechCo needs EU+US scope. Per our internal review, here’s the proposed workflow and customer-facing language we recommend: 

Proposed workflow (summary):
1) Customer calls delete API -> logical deletion from live storage within minutes.
2) Index compaction scheduled (account-level) -> tombstones physically removed within 6 hours.
3) Replica sync completes (if cross-region) -> up to 2 hours.
4) Daily snapshots are retained for 30 days by default.
   - Expedited option: raise an ops ticket to run an accelerated snapshot prune; typical completion 3–7 business days.
   - Alternate option (if customer-managed KMS): revoke CMK to render older backups inaccessible. This is an irreversible action and must be agreed in writing.

Requested from FintechCo:
- Please confirm you want the expedited snapshot purge for both EU and US and provide a signed request authorizing ops to prune snapshots.
- If you prefer CMK revocation as the remediation path, confirm in writing and we’ll route to legal/ops to document risks.

I’ve attached a short timeline spreadsheet (DB_Purge_Timeline.xlsx) and a one-pager RTBF_Process_Summary.pdf for your legal team. If it helps, I can set up a technical deep-dive with our infra lead to walk through snapshots and KMS specifics.
